title: Integral monoid pushout along a submonoid to a group embeds in a group
statement:
Let $P$ be a commutative monoid, written multiplicatively, whose canonical map to its group completion $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ (the monoid algebra construction in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]) is injective. Here the group completion is the abelian group obtained by formally adjoining inverses, with its universal homomorphism from $P$. Let $E\subseteq P$ be a submonoid and let $f:E\to G$ be a monoid homomorphism to an abelian group $G$, with no injectivity assumption on $f$. Define $M=P\oplus_E G$ as the quotient of $P\times G$ by the monoid congruence generated by $(pe,g)\sim(p,f(e)g)$ for $e\in E$. Write $f^{\mathrm{gp}}:E^{\mathrm{gp}}\to G$ for the extension, and regard $E^{\mathrm{gp}}$ as a subgroup of $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. Put
$$H=(P^{\mathrm{gp}}\times G)/\{(z,f^{\mathrm{gp}}(z)^{-1}):z\in E^{\mathrm{gp}}\}.$$
The homomorphism $M\to H$ induced by $(p,g)\mapsto[(p,g)]$ is injective. In particular $M$ embeds in its group completion and is cancellative. The canonical map $G\to M$, $g\mapsto[1,g]$, is injective, and its multiplication action on $M$ is free. For $p,p'\in P$ and $g,g'\in G$, equality $[p,g]=[p',g']$ holds if and only if there exist $e,e'\in E$ such that
$$pe'=p'e\quad\hbox{and}\quad g f(e)=g'f(e').$$

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, integral-monoid localization convention only. Agent-formulated mixed pushout embedding and equality criterion, used in XVI Proposition 3.6.3 chart argument, p.252; not a theorem asserted in ILO. WANTED: Kato (1988), section 1, associated-log algebra.

proof.text: The formula $(p,g)\mapsto[(p,g)]$ respects each defining relation: in $H$ the quotient identifies $(pe,g)$ with $(p,f(e)g)$ because their ratio is $(e,f(e)^{-1})$, the image of $e\in E\subseteq E^{\rm gp}$. It therefore induces a monoid homomorphism $M\to H$.

source.place: Agent elementary verification of the mixed pushout; Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, supplies the integral-monoid group-completion convention

proof.text: First justify the subgroup convention in the statement directly from the group presentation in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. In $P^{\rm gp}$ the fractions $ee'^{-1}$ with $e,e'\in E$ form a subgroup $L$. Equality $ee'^{-1}=dd'^{-1}$ gives $ed'=de'$ in $P$, by injectivity of $P\to P^{\rm gp}$, hence also in its submonoid $E$. Thus any homomorphism $u:E\to K$ to an abelian group extends uniquely to $L$ by $ee'^{-1}\mapsto u(e)u(e')^{-1}$: the cross equality makes this well-defined, multiplication of fractions makes it a homomorphism, and the fractions generate $L$. This identifies $E^{\rm gp}$ with $L$ and gives $f^{\rm gp}(ee'^{-1})=f(e)f(e')^{-1}$. Now equality of the images of $(p,g)$ and $(p',g')$ in $H$ says $(pp'^{-1},gg'^{-1})=(z,f^{\rm gp}(z)^{-1})$ for some $z\in E^{\rm gp}$. Writing $z=ee'^{-1}$ and using again injectivity of $P\to P^{\rm gp}$ gives exactly $pe'=p'e$ and $g f(e)=g'f(e')$.

source.place: Agent elementary verification of the mixed pushout; Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, supplies the integral-monoid group-completion convention

proof.text: Conversely, if $e,e^{'}\in E$ satisfy $pe^{'}=p^{'}e$ and $g f(e)=g^{'}f(e^{'})$, then $(pp^{'-1},gg^{'-1})=(ee^{'-1},f(e^{'})f(e)^{-1})=(ee^{'-1},f^{\rm gp}(ee^{'-1})^{-1})$. This is one of the subgroup elements quotiented out in the definition of $H$, so $[p,g]=[p^{'},g^{'}]$ in $H$.

source.place: Agent elementary verification of the mixed pushout; Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, supplies the integral-monoid group-completion convention

proof.text: The same criterion proves equality in $M$. The defining relation gives $[p,g]=[pe^{'},f(e^{'})^{-1}g]$ and $[p^{'},g^{'}]=[p^{'}e,f(e)^{-1}g^{'}]$. The displayed equations imply $f(e^{'})^{-1}g=f(e)^{-1}g^{'}$, while $pe^{'}=p^{'}e$, so these two representatives are equal. Thus equality in $H$ already implies equality in $M$, and the induced map $M\to H$ is injective.

source.place: Agent elementary verification of the mixed pushout; Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, supplies the integral-monoid group-completion convention

proof.text: For the canonical map $G\to M$, apply the criterion to $[1,g]=[1,g^{'}]$. It gives $e^{'}=e$ and then $g f(e)=g^{'}f(e)$, hence $g=g^{'}$ by cancellation in the group $G$. If $h\in G$ fixes $[p,g]$, apply the criterion to $[p,hg]=[p,g]$; it gives $pe^{'}=pe$, hence $e^{'}=e$ by the injectivity of $P\to P^{\rm gp}$, and then $hg f(e)=g f(e)$, so $h=1$. Therefore the action is free.

source.place: Agent elementary verification of the mixed pushout; Expose VIII 3.1.2, printed p.98, supplies the integral-monoid group-completion convention

proof.text: Write $j:M\to H$ for the injective homomorphism proved in Step 4. The group presentation of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives a homomorphism $\widetilde j:M^{\rm gp}\to H$ by sending each generator $[m]$ to $j(m)$: the relation $[mm']=[m][m']$ is respected because $j$ is multiplicative. Its composite with the canonical map $\iota:M\to M^{\rm gp}$ is $j$. If $\iota(b)=\iota(c)$, applying $\widetilde j$ gives $j(b)=j(c)$ and hence $b=c$. This proves the claimed embedding into the group completion. Finally, if $ab=ac$ in $M$, their images in the group $H$ give $j(a)j(b)=j(a)j(c)$; cancelling $j(a)$ and using injectivity of $j$ gives $b=c$. Thus $M$ is cancellative.

source.place: Agent elementary consequence of the embedding into a group
